queue.name: sisyphean
queue.descr: The mindset associated with this is called "Sisyphean" thinking or the Sisyphean condition, which refers to: Endless, futile effort with no meaningful progress Feeling trapped in repetitive, thankless work The sense that no matter how hard you try, you're back to square one Albert Camus famously reframed it in his essay The Myth of Sisyphus (1942), arguing that we must imagine Sisyphus happy — finding meaning in the struggle itself rather than the outcome.  This became a cornerstone of existentialist/absurdist philosophy. In modern psychology, it connects to concepts like learned helplessness or burnout — when effort feels perpetually disconnected from results.
